title: The Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem in the Basic Cohen Model

items.title: Schema of continuity in the basic Cohen model
items.statement: Let V satisfy ZF, let G be generic for Add(omega,omega), let A={a_i:i in omega} be the set of coordinate Cohen reals, and let x be a finite tuple from V. If s is a finite tuple of distinct members of A and V[G] satisfies phi(x,s,A), then pairwise disjoint basic clopen neighbourhoods U_j of the coordinates of s can be chosen so that V[G] satisfies phi(x,t,A) for every tuple t of members of A with t_j in U_j. Consequently, parameters ordinal-definable from A and a fixed finite support tuple may be held fixed while a finite tuple of distinct members of A, disjoint from that support tuple, is varied in such neighbourhoods.
items.strategy: Use the forcing truth lemma to choose a condition forcing the displayed instance. Strengthen it to a finite square whose rows have pairwise incompatible initial segments. If a tuple in the resulting clopen box made the formula false, use the truth lemma again and a finite permutation of Cohen indices to move its rows onto the original rows. The permuted countercondition is compatible with the square condition, while the symmetry lemma makes the two compatible conditions force opposite statements. For the consequence, replace each supported parameter by its ordinal definition, apply the ground-parameter case to the concatenation of its finite support and the tuple being varied, and then keep the support coordinates fixed.

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free inside the stated symmetric-model setup; only finite supports, finite permutations and finite extensions are chosen.

items.title: Finite parameter sets admit disjoint clopen supports
items.statement: In the basic Cohen model, let B and a finite-arity map d on tuples of distinct members of A be ordinal-definable from A and a finite support tuple f from A. Given finitely many input tuples whose combined coordinates form a finite set F disjoint from rng(f), and any fixed finite conjunction of assertions that values d(t) or their Boolean complements belong or do not belong to fixed supported sets such as B or an ideal I, there are pairwise disjoint basic clopen neighbourhoods distinguishing F, all disjoint from rng(f), such that every coordinatewise substitution from A through those neighbourhoods preserves the entire conjunction.
items.strategy: Replace B, d and the fixed supported sets by their ordinal definitions from A and f, and apply the continuity schema to the finite conjunction with the concatenated tuple f followed by an enumeration of F. Retain the clopens belonging to F and shrink them inside any previously prescribed basic clopens. Their pairwise disjointness keeps all substituted coordinates distinct. No countable or global choice is used.

items.title: A supported Boolean algebra has an ideal maximal in its supported-definability class
items.statement: Let B be a nontrivial Boolean algebra in the basic Cohen model that is ordinal-definable from A and a fixed finite tuple f. Then B has a proper ideal I which is maximal among the proper ideals of B that are ordinal-definable from A and f; I itself is ordinal-definable from A and f.
items.strategy: Use the canonical definable well-order of OD(A,f) to enumerate the proper ideals of B that are OD(A,f). By transfinite recursion maintain an increasing proper ideal: at a successor stage replace the current ideal by the enumerated ideal exactly when the latter contains it, and at limits take unions. The union is proper because membership of 1 would already occur at one stage. If an OD(A,f) proper ideal strictly extended the result, its own stage would have absorbed it, a contradiction. This is definable recursion, not Zorn or AC.

items.title: Search-and-shift prime-ideal construction in the basic Cohen model
items.statement: For the finite-support basic Cohen symmetric system over a transitive ZFC ground, every proper set filter in the hereditarily symmetric model extends there to an ultrafilter; consequently every nontrivial Boolean algebra there has a prime ideal.
items.strategy: Follow the Halpern–Lévy search-and-shift proof in its modern symmetric-extension form. Establish minimal supports, the finite compatible-type and Erdős–Rado product thinnings, and the large-index filter-extension property; compare countable and large index through the exact Sigma/Gamma maps and an outer collapse; then enumerate canonical nice subset names in the ground and build the internal ultrafilter. This stays in the HS presentation and avoids the defective maximal-parameter-definable-ideal inference.

items.statement: The basic Cohen symmetric model is a model of ZF in which the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem holds and the Axiom of Choice fails.
items.strategy: Combine the HS search-and-shift filter-extension theorem with the general symmetric-model ZF theorem and the Dedekind-finite Cohen orbit witnessing failure of Choice. The whole proof stays in the hereditarily symmetric presentation.

items.title: Relative consistency of BPI without Choice over ZF
items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF+BPI+not-AC is consistent. Consequently BPI does not imply AC over ZF.
items.strategy: Assume a particular finite target refutation, extract its externally fixed finite ZF fragment, and combine the fixed-fragment basic Cohen construction with the fixed finite search-and-shift proof of BPI. Relativizing that one refutation to the resulting set model contradicts source consistency. This proves the external syntactic consistency implication without claiming a PA-uniform proof transformer.

title: The Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem in the Basic Cohen Model — Examples

items.title: The finite Boolean expansion contradiction in the supported-ideal proof
items.statement: Let I be a proper ideal of a Boolean algebra B, let y be finite and let d:y->B. If every truth-assignment atom formed from the d(a)'s belongs to I, then the finite Boolean expansion of 1 puts 1 in I, a contradiction. In the unary disjoint-clopen pattern used by the supported-ideal proof, print the two exhaustive cases which would supply those atom memberships; do not assert that the unresolved primality lemma has supplied the pattern.
items.strategy: For z contained in y define e_z as the meet of d(a) for a in z and complements for a in y minus z. Prove by induction on the finite set y that the join of all e_z is 1, including y empty. Under the printed clopen-pattern hypotheses, if z meets every top-level clopen then its positive meet is in I, while if it misses one then the complementary meet over y minus z is in I; downward closure puts e_z in I in either case. Finite join closure then contradicts propriety. This is a conditional finite calculation and does not discharge the missing construction in the A-page primality lemma.

items.title: BPI is equivalent to the Axiom of Choice
items.statement: False: the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem is equivalent to the Axiom of Choice.
items.strategy: AC proves BPI, while the certified syntactic relative-consistency theorem gives, conditional on Con(ZF), consistency of ZF+BPI+not-AC. This refutes only the reverse implication and does not infer a transitive model from bare consistency.

items.title: The Feferman–Levy symmetric collapse system
items.statement: Work over a transitive ground model V of ZFC+GCH. For each n in omega let kappa_n=aleph_n^V. Let P consist of finite sets of triples (n,i,alpha), with i in omega and alpha<kappa_n, functional in (n,i), ordered by reverse inclusion. Let G preserve each first coordinate n while permuting the i-coordinates independently; let H_m fix every layer n<m pointwise and let F be the normal filter generated by the H_m. The associated hereditarily symmetric interpretation is the Feferman-Levy model N.
items.strategy: This fixes the exact forcing, layer-preserving automorphism group, bounded-initial-layer supports, normal filter and symmetric model before any collapse calculation. Conditions are finite partial collapse functions, not Cohen-bit conditions and not the published one-cardinal Levy-collapse notation.

references.title: Thomas Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.axiom_audit: The construction starts in ZFC+GCH; AC is declared for the ground aleph sequence and GCH cardinal calculation. The symmetric target model will satisfy ZF without AC.

items.title: Hereditarily symmetric names have bounded layer support
items.statement: Every hereditarily symmetric name in the Feferman-Levy system is fixed by H_m for some m; in particular every real in N has a name whose Boolean values are fixed by one bounded initial-layer stabilizer H_m.
items.strategy: Unpack membership in the normal filter generated by the descending H_m. For a real in the supplied generic, form the standard Boolean name from the atomic membership values and use the truth lemma to prove value equality in that generic; automorphism invariance preserves the same layer bound.

references.title: Thomas Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free after the symmetric system is fixed.

items.title: Fixed Boolean values come from initial collapse layers
items.statement: Let B=RO(P), and let B_m be the complete subalgebra of Boolean values fixed by H_m. If u is in B_m, then u is the join of the initial-layer restrictions p restricted to m over all conditions p below u. Hence B_m is exactly the completion generated by conditions using layers n<m.
items.strategy: If p is below u but p restricted to m is not, choose q extending p restricted to m below the complement of u. A permutation in H_m can move the finitely many upper-layer i-coordinates of q away from those of p, so the moved q is compatible with p. Since u is H_m-fixed, this contradicts that p is below u and the moved q below its complement.

references.title: Thomas Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free finite fresh-coordinate permutation.

items.title: The real layers of the Feferman–Levy model
items.statement: For m in omega, let S_m be the set of nice P-names for subsets of omega whose Boolean values lie in B_m, and let R_m be the interpretation in N of the canonical symmetric name collecting S_m. Thus R_m is the set of reals admitting an m-bounded name.
items.strategy: The preceding Boolean-value lemma makes S_m invariant under the full layer-preserving group, so the canonical name for R_m and the sequence m maps to R_m are hereditarily symmetric.

references.title: Thomas Jech, The Axiom of Choice
references.locator: Definitions of S_n and R_n and equation (10.8), pp.143-144

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free definition.

items.title: Each real layer has a ground-model cardinal bound
items.statement: In the Feferman-Levy model, R_m has cardinality at most aleph_{m+1}^V (indeed Jech's GCH calculation gives equality).
items.strategy: By the initial-layer Boolean representation, a nice real name in S_m is coded by a countable sequence of subsets of the set of initial-layer conditions. Under ground-model GCH that set and its relevant power set have size aleph_{m+1}^V. The coding well-order descends to a surjection from aleph_{m+1}^V onto R_m; only the upper bound is consumed later.

references.title: Thomas Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.axiom_audit: Ground-model AC+GCH is used for the aleph cardinal computation; no choice sequence is asserted inside N.

items.title: Every finite ground aleph is countable in the Feferman–Levy model
items.statement: For every n in omega, the ground-model ordinal aleph_n^V is countable in N.
items.strategy: The generic union in layer n is a surjection from omega onto aleph_n^V. Its canonical name is fixed by H_{n+1}, hence is hereditarily symmetric and belongs to N. Verify totality and surjectivity by the standard dense sets for the finite partial collapse forcing.

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free in N: the individual surjections are canonical generic objects. No simultaneous choice of enumerations is made.

items.title: Each Feferman–Levy real layer is countable
items.statement: For every m in omega, R_m is countable in N.
items.strategy: Use countability of the nonempty ordinal aleph_{m+1}^V and the choice-free countable-surjection equivalence to fix one internal surjection from omega, then compose it with the supplied map onto R_m. This is one existential witness for one fixed m, not a choice of a family of enumerations.

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free; for one fixed layer, existential elimination fixes one surjection. No simultaneous choice of enumerations is made.

items.title: The Feferman–Levy reals are a countable union of countable sets
items.statement: In N, R=union_{m in omega} R_m and every R_m is countable. Thus the set of all reals is a countable union of countable sets.
items.strategy: Bounded support puts each real into some R_m. The canonical symmetric sequence m maps to R_m supplies the countable family as a set of N, and the preceding lemma proves each member countable. Do not infer that the union is countable: assembling enumerations uniformly is exactly what fails.

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free theorem in N.

items.title: The Feferman–Levy reals remain uncountable
items.statement: The real line of N is uncountable even though it is the union of the countable sequence (R_m)_{m in omega} of countable sets.
items.strategy: Apply the ZF theorem that R is uncountable inside the ZF model N. This establishes the required contrast without any appeal to AC or to a recorded Feferman-Levy remark.

references.title: Thomas Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.axiom_audit: Choice-free Cantor diagonal argument.

items.title: The new omega one is the old aleph omega
items.statement: In the Feferman-Levy model N, omega_1^N equals aleph_omega^V.
items.strategy: Every ordinal below aleph_omega^V lies below some ground aleph_n and is countable in N, so aleph_omega^V is at most omega_1^N. Conversely, if a hereditarily symmetric name gave a surjection from omega onto aleph_omega^V, choose m supporting it. The fixed-Boolean-value lemma replaces each deciding condition by its restriction to the first m layers. Under GCH there are only aleph_m^V such restrictions, so the union of the ranges decided by the countably many coordinates has ground size at most aleph_m^V and cannot cover aleph_omega^V. Hence aleph_omega^V stays uncountable and is the least uncountable ordinal.

references.title: Thomas Jech, The Axiom of Choice

items.axiom_audit: Ground AC+GCH supplies the cardinal bound on initial-layer conditions. The conclusion is internal to the choice-free model N.

items.title: The Feferman–Levy omega one has countable cofinality
items.statement: In N, cf(omega_1)=omega.
items.strategy: The sequence n maps to aleph_n^V belongs to N and is cofinal in aleph_omega^V=omega_1^N. Since omega_1 is a limit ordinal and cannot have finite cofinality, its cofinality is exactly omega.

items.title: Countable-union and omega-one regularity principles fail
items.statement: In N, the assertion that every countable union of countable sets is countable is false, omega_1 is singular, and Countable Choice fails.
items.strategy: The countable real-layer decomposition and ZF uncountability refute the union principle. Countable cofinality refutes regularity. The published implication AC_omega=>cf(omega_1)=omega_1 then gives not-AC_omega by contraposition.

items.title: The Feferman–Levy collapse argument is finitely formalizable
items.statement: For every externally fixed finite fragment Delta of ZF plus the three conclusions in the preceding corollary, ZFC+GCH proves that a set model of Delta is obtained by the Feferman-Levy symmetric collapse construction.
items.strategy: Collect the finitely many forcing, symmetry, Replacement and Separation instances used by Delta and by the layer, cardinal and cofinality arguments above. Reflection supplies a suitable set-sized source; forcing and the symmetry recursion construct the set model. The quantification over Delta is external, so no uniform satisfaction predicate or countable transitive model is asserted.

items.title: Relative consistency of the Feferman–Levy choice failures over ZF
items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF is consistent with the reals being a countable union of countable sets, cf(omega_1)=omega, and failure of Countable Choice.
items.strategy: From Con(ZF), use formal consistency transfer to ZFC+GCH. Apply the finite-fragment formalization to every finite target fragment and compactness to obtain consistency of the full displayed ZF theory.

items.title: The tail-flip hereditary-symmetric model
items.statement: Work over a transitive ground model V of ZFC+V=L and force with Add(omega,omega), writing (S_n)_{n in omega} for the coordinate Cohen subsets of omega. Let the ground-model bit-flip group act on omega times omega, let H_m forbid flips on rows below m, and let F be the normal filter generated by the H_m. Define F_tf as the interpretation of the hereditarily symmetric names. Each individual HS name has some support H_m. No uniform H_m for its transitive closure, finite-predicate definition of every HS object, or equality with a literal hereditary fixed-stage union is asserted.
items.strategy: Verify directly that the all-bit flip action and bounded-row stabilizers form a symmetric system, then record exactly the finite-support consequence H_m subseteq sym(dot x) for one HS name. A coordinate-m tail flip shows that the literal union of hereditary fixed finite-predicate stages would contain every S_n but could not contain its own power set of omega, so that union is not the model. Feferman's source model M* is identified separately as a transfinite ramified hierarchy rather than with F_tf.

items.title: The tail-flip hereditary-symmetric interpretation is a model of ZF
items.statement: The tail-flip hereditary-symmetric interpretation F_tf is a transitive inner model of ZF of the generic extension V[G].
items.strategy: Apply the library's general theorem that the hereditary-symmetric interpretation of a symmetric system is a transitive ZF model. The legacy identifier records the connection to Feferman's tail transform, while the proof explicitly distinguishes this HS construction from Feferman's ramified M* and from the false literal fixed-stage union.

items.title: The tail-complement automorphism fixes finitely supported names
items.statement: Let dot x be an HS name supported by H_m, let Q be a finite condition, and choose r at least m. Past the finitely many row-r bits mentioned by Q, the automorphism that flips the entire tail of row r fixes Q and dot x while sending S_r to its complement modulo a finite initial segment.
items.strategy: Choose k_0 above the finite row-r domain of Q and use the corresponding ground-model tail bit set. The resulting automorphism lies in H_m, so it fixes the supported name; it misses dom(Q), so it fixes Q; and its action on S_r is exact complementation beyond k_0. The infinite tail is load-bearing because a finite flip preserves membership in every free ultrafilter under finite modification.

items.title: Every prime ideal on the power set of omega is principal in the tail-flip symmetric model
items.statement: In F_tf, every prime ideal of the internal Boolean algebra P(omega) is principal.
items.strategy: Represent a hypothetical nonprincipal prime ideal by an HS name and choose H_m inside its stabilizer. Such an ideal contains every finite subset of omega. Primality decides the supported coordinate set S_m; a condition forces one decision. The row-m infinite tail flip fixes both that condition and the ideal name while carrying the decided set to its complement modulo finite. Closure then puts a set and its complement in the ideal, contradicting propriety.

items.title: The tail-flip symmetric model has no free ultrafilter on omega
items.statement: Every ultrafilter on omega in F_tf is principal; in particular the tail-flip symmetric model has no free ultrafilter on omega.
items.strategy: Complementation identifies ultrafilters on omega with prime ideals of P(omega). Apply the preceding theorem, then prove that a principal prime ideal of P(omega) must be generated by the complement of one point; complementation gives the corresponding point-principal ultrafilter.

items.title: The tail-flip symmetric model refutes BPI
items.statement: The Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem and the equivalent set Ultrafilter Lemma fail in F_tf.
items.strategy: The ideal Fin of finite subsets of omega is a proper ideal of P(omega). A prime ideal extending Fin would be nonprincipal, contradicting the prime-ideal theorem above. Equivalently the cofinite filter has no ultrafilter extension. Invoke the published equivalence only after the concrete witness is established.

items.title: The tail-flip symmetric model is finitely formalizable

items.title: Relative consistency of no free ultrafilter on omega over ZF
items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF is consistent with every ultrafilter on omega being principal and with failure of BPI.
items.strategy: Transfer Con(ZF) to Con(ZFC+GCH), then argue against a hypothetical finite target refutation. The tail-flip HS formalization supplies a set model of exactly the finitely many ZF instances and two target sentences used by that refutation, contradicting finite first-order soundness. The proof does not identify the target with Feferman's ramified M* and does not assert that a CTM of full ZF exists.

items.title: The Ultrafilter Lemma and BPI are not theorems of ZF
items.statement: Assuming Con(ZF), neither the set Ultrafilter Lemma nor the Boolean Prime Ideal Theorem is provable in ZF.
items.strategy: The preceding relative-consistency model refutes BPI and the equivalent Ultrafilter Lemma. If ZF proved either principle, every model of ZF would satisfy it, contradicting consistency of the displayed countermodel.

items.title: Blass's finite-modification classes and parameter-HOD model
items.statement: Over a countable transitive M satisfying ZF+V=L, add Cohen reals a_n by Fn(omega times omega,2). For x subset omega let delta(x) be its finite-symmetric-difference class, put f(n)={delta(a_n),delta(omega minus a_n)}, and let S be the union of all those classes together with {f}. Blass's model is N=HOD(S), equivalently the sets hereditarily ordinal-definable from f and finitely many members of S.
items.strategy: Fix the forcing, the paired finite-modification classes, the parameter set and the finite-parameter HOD convention. Tachtsis reproduces this construction and checks the canonical tail-flip names; it does not reproduce Blass's all-ultrafilters theorem.

references.title: Eleftherios Tachtsis, On the Existence of Free Ultrafilters on omega and on Russell-sets in ZF

items.axiom_audit: Ambient source-model choice is declared. The parameter-HOD target is intended to satisfy ZF without AC.

items.title: Blass's paired finite-modification classes form a Russell set
items.statement: In Blass's parameter-HOD model, the countable family ({delta(a_n),delta(omega minus a_n)})_{n in omega} has no infinite partial choice function; hence its union is a Russell set.
items.strategy: Assume a partial choice function is definable from f, ordinals and finitely many class parameters. Choose a fresh k outside their indices and a condition deciding a selected class at k. Flip every sufficiently late bit of a_k. The automorphism fixes the condition, f and all parameters but interchanges delta(a_k) with delta(omega minus a_k), contradicting functionality.

items.title: Small forcing does not create measurable cardinals
items.statement: Assume ZFC. If V[G] is a generic extension by a forcing notion in V of cardinality less than an uncountable cardinal kappa, then kappa carries a nonprincipal kappa-complete ultrafilter in V[G] only if it already carries one in V. The proof locally constructs the normal ultrapower embedding and the converse seed measure.
items.strategy: Define measurability locally through nonprincipal kappa-complete ultrafilters. Prove the required ultrapower, normalization, closure, and seed-measure facts directly, then regard the forcing as gap forcing with a trivial closed tail. The gap restriction argument puts the restricted target and embedding in V, and the seed derives a ground measure.

items.title: Every ultrafilter on every set is principal in Blass's model
items.statement: In Blass's parameter-HOD model N, every ultrafilter on every set is principal.
items.strategy: Split the proof into four explicit reductions. First, the finite-parameter HOD class is a transitive ZF model, and a fresh-coordinate tail-complement automorphism rules out a free ultrafilter on omega. Second, if kappa is the least ordinal carrying a free ultrafilter, the least partition of kappa into small pieces has length kappa, so the ultrafilter is uniform and kappa-complete. Tail homogeneity traces it to a kappa-complete nonprincipal ultrafilter in the finite-coordinate ZFC extension generated by its real parameters. The preceding Levy-Solovay theorem then reflects measurability to L, contradicting Scott's V=L argument. Third, for W the least class containing every singleton and closed under well-ordered unions, prove closure under subsets, finite products and surjective images; use bounded definition codes rather than a choice of witnesses to prove N=W. Finally induct on W-rank, refine a well-ordered union to its least-index partition, and push any ultrafilter to the indexing ordinal. Principality there concentrates it on one lower-rank piece, where induction applies.

items.title: The Blass ultrafilter-free construction is finitely formalizable
items.statement: For every externally fixed finite fragment Delta of ZF plus the assertion that every ultrafilter on every set is principal, a suitable finite ZFC source proves that Blass's parameter-HOD construction yields a set model of Delta.
items.strategy: For an externally fixed finite Delta, collect the finitely many instances used in: the Cohen forcing theorem and parameter-HOD construction; the fresh-coordinate tail-complement contradiction on omega; the least-ordinal partition and finite-coordinate homogeneity trace; the no-new-measurables gap-forcing proof and Scott's V=L contradiction; the W-rank proof that HOD(S)=W; and the W-rank induction for arbitrary ultrafilters. Reflection supplies a set-sized source satisfying the needed finite ZFC+V=L fragment, and the forcing and definability recursions construct a set model of Delta. The external quantification over Delta avoids an internal truth predicate or a countable-transitive-model assumption.

items.statement: If ZF is consistent, then ZF is consistent with every ultrafilter on every set being principal.

items.title: Finite bit flips cannot defeat a free ultrafilter
items.statement: A finite modification of a subset of omega has exactly the same membership status in every free ultrafilter, so a finite-bit flip cannot yield Feferman's contradiction.
items.strategy: A free ultrafilter contains every cofinite set and no finite set. If X symmetric-difference Y is finite, intersect X with the cofinite agreement set to prove X is in U iff Y is in U. This directly exposes the defect in the published recorded remark's finite-flip explanation.
